title: Implement POST /api/crawl endpoint on Express
description: Implement the main scraping endpoint on the Express sidecar server. Accepts a URL and optional maxPages, runs the Crawlee crawler, extracts page data and branding, and returns structured JSON. This is called by the Next.js app's pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/crawl accepts `{ url: string, maxPages?: number }` in request body
Returns `{ success: true, pages: PageData[], branding: BrandingData }` on success
Returns `{ success: false, error: string }` with 400 if URL is missing or invalid
Returns `{ success: false, error: string }` with 500 on crawl failure
URL is validated before crawling (must be a valid http/https URL)
maxPages defaults to 10 if not provided
Endpoint handles concurrent requests without collision (each crawl is isolated)

steps.description: Add POST /api/crawl route handler in server.ts
steps.details: In `src/scraper/server.ts`, import `crawlSite` from `./crawlee-service` and `extractPageData` from `./extract`. Register: `app.post('/api/crawl', async (req, res) => { ... })`.

Check that `req.body.url` exists and is a valid URL. Use `new URL(req.body.url)` wrapped in try/catch. If invalid, return `res.status(400).json({ success: false, error: 'Invalid URL' })`. Check protocol is http or https.

Call `crawlSite(url, maxPages)` to get raw pages. For each raw page, call `extractPageData($, url, rawHtml)` to produce a `PageData` object. Run `extractBranding(homepageRawHtml, url)` on the first page. Return `{ success: true, pages, branding }`.

With the Express server running, send a test request: `curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/crawl -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"url":"https://example.com","maxPages":3}'`. Verify the response contains `success: true`, a `pages` array, and a `branding` object.

technicalNotes: Each crawl uses its own Crawlee storage context to avoid collisions between concurrent requests.
The endpoint is only called from localhost (Next.js app on port 3000) so no authentication is needed.
Log request start/end with timing for debugging: `console.log('Crawling', url, '- completed in', elapsed, 'ms')`
